findings.title: Materials' 54% multiple compression is a bet on a 120% earnings surge
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.68x forward versus 38.81x trailing, a 54 percent compression that implies analysts expect next-12m earnings to grow 120 percent. That is an extraordinary underwriting of margin recovery, especially when the forward multiple sits at only the 44th percentile of its five-year range while the trailing multiple is at the 93rd.

findings.title: Information Technology's forward multiple is historically cheap despite rich trailing
findings.body: IT's forward P/E of 21.66 sits at the 11th percentile of its five-year range, yet its trailing P/E of 36.70 is at the 52nd. The 41-point gap between lenses reflects a 69 percent expected earnings jump, but the market is pricing that growth at a level rarely seen in the last five years.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward multiple collapsed while trailing stayed flat
findings.body: Real Estate's forward P/E fell 15 percentile points in a week and 16 in a month, landing at 36.39x with a 36th-percentile rank, while its trailing multiple of 34.76x sits at the 30th percentile. The forward lens now implies a 4 percent earnings decline, a sharp reversal from the optimism that had been embedded just weeks ago.
